\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{فاوض} (fāwaḍa)}{فاوض (fāwaḍa)}]{\ar{فاوض} (fāwaḍa) — to hold talks (with); to negotiate}

\label{lesson:AR-C524-fawada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an evaluation, then the Arabic for production.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{فاوض}}
\textbf{\ar{فاوض}} — \emph{fāwaḍa} — \textquotedblleft{}to hold talks (with); to negotiate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{فاوض} \ar{العمال} \ar{المدير} \ar{على} \ar{الأجر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{fāwaḍa al-ʿummāl al-mudīr ʿalā al-ajr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The workers negotiated their pay with the manager.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يفاوض}, \emph{yufāwiḍ}.

It takes \ar{على} for the matter.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{فاوض}} (\emph{fāwaḍa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-w-ḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}to entrust, to share in\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Form III fāwaḍa is to talk a matter through with someone.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fāwaḍa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fāwaḍa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fāwaḍa al-ʿummāl al-mudīr ʿalā al-ajr.} — The workers negotiated their pay with the manager.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an evaluation, then the Arabic for production, then say \emph{fāwaḍa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{فاوض} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To hold talks (with); to negotiate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اجتهد} (ijtahada)}{اجتهد (ijtahada)}]{\ar{اجتهد} (ijtahada) — to work hard, to strive}

\label{lesson:AR-C524-ijtahada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for production, then the Arabic for to hold talks.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اجتهد}}
\textbf{\ar{اجتهد}} — \emph{ijtahada} — \textquotedblleft{}to work hard, to strive\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اجتهد} \ar{الطالب} \ar{ونجح} \ar{في} \ar{الامتحان}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ijtahada aṭ-ṭālib wa-najaḥa fī al-imtiḥān.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The student worked hard and passed the exam.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يجتهد}, \emph{yajtahid}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اجتهد}} (\emph{ijtahada}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-h-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to strive, to exert oneself\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Mujtahid, hard-working, which you know, is its participle.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ijtahada}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ijtahada aṭ-ṭālib wa-najaḥa fī al-imtiḥān.} — The student worked hard and passed the exam.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for production, then the Arabic for to hold talks, then say \emph{ijtahada} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ناوب} (nāwaba)}{ناوب (nāwaba)}]{\ar{ناوب} (nāwaba) — to be on duty; to take turns}

\label{lesson:AR-C524-nawaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to hold talks, then the Arabic for to work hard.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ناوب}}
\textbf{\ar{ناوب}} — \emph{nāwaba} — \textquotedblleft{}to be on duty; to take turns\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يناوب} \ar{الطبيب} \ar{في} \ar{المستشفى} \ar{مرة} \ar{كل} \ar{أسبوع}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yunāwibu aṭ-ṭabīb fī al-mustashfā marra kull usbūʿ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor is on duty at the hospital once a week.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يناوب}, \emph{yunāwib}.

Munāwaba, a shift, is its verbal noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ناوب}} (\emph{nāwaba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-w-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to come in turn\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Form III nāwaba is to take one's turn.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yunāwibu aṭ-ṭabīb fī al-mustashfā marra kull usbūʿ.} — The doctor is on duty at the hospital once a week.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to hold talks, then the Arabic for to work hard, then say \emph{nāwaba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ترقى} (taraqqā)}{ترقى (taraqqā)}]{\ar{ترقى} (taraqqā) — to be promoted}

\label{lesson:AR-C524-taraqqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to work hard, then the Arabic for to be on duty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ترقى}}
\textbf{\ar{ترقى}} — \emph{taraqqā} — \textquotedblleft{}to be promoted\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ترقى} \ar{خالي} \ar{في} \ar{الشركة} \ar{بسرعة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taraqqā khālī fī ash-sharika bi-surʿa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My uncle was promoted quickly in the company.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يترقى}, \emph{yataraqqā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ترقى}} (\emph{taraqqā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-q-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to go up, to climb\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Form V taraqqā is to rise step by step.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to work hard, then the Arabic for to be on duty, then say \emph{taraqqā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مقر} (maqarr)}{مقر (maqarr)}]{\ar{مقر} (maqarr) — headquarters, a base}

\label{lesson:AR-C524-maqarr}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to be on duty, then the Arabic for to be promoted.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مقر}}
\textbf{\ar{مقر}} — \emph{maqarr} — \textquotedblleft{}headquarters, a base\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{مقر} \ar{الشركة} \ar{في} \ar{وسط} \ar{المدينة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maqarr ash-sharika fī wasaṭ al-madīna.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The company's headquarters is in the city centre.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مقر}} (\emph{maqarr}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-r-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to settle, to stay firm\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A maqarr is a place where a thing settles.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maqarr}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to be on duty, then the Arabic for to be promoted, then say \emph{maqarr} again
\end{itemize}
